In mathematics, a '''metasymplectic space''', introduced  by {{harvs|txt|last=Freudenthal|year=1959}} and {{harvtxt|Tits|1974|loc=10.13}}, is a [[Tits building]] of type F4 (a specific generalized [[incidence structure]]).
The four types of vertices are called  points, lines, planes, and symplecta.
